Subject: MAP kickoff — performance evaluation scope and close timeline

Samir / Priya,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — great discussion. Per our MAP (attached redwood_map_v1.pdf), we want to align on a short evaluation plan focused on the performance metrics that matter to ACME:

- TTFT (time-to-first-token) at 95th and 99th percentiles
- Median and p95 per-token latency across sequences
- Sustained throughput (tokens/sec) at target concurrency levels (4, 8, 16)
- Concurrency behavior (latency amplification and tail behavior)

Proposed short timeline:
1) Week of Mar 23: ACME runs first-pass tests using their internal harness and shares logs (acme_test_logs.zip)
2) Mar 25: Redwood repro attempt + methodology alignment call if divergences appear
3) Mar 30: Final MAP signoff and recommended production config (quantization/batching/route) — this aligns with your quarter-end close target

A couple of asks: please attach one representative request payload (typical prompt + max_tokens) and the exact harness you use (k6/locust/custom). If you can capture the raw request timestamps and server-side request ids, that will make matching easier.

I'll loop in our performance SME (Rishi) and the solutions engineer (Connor) to help reproduce and triage.

Best,
Neha Kapoor
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Neha — appreciate the clear scope. We ran a quick pass over the weekend and attached the trimmed logs (acme_test_logs.zip). High level observations:

- Using k6 with 50 virtual users, steady ramp to 8 concurrent requests produced sustained ~420 tokens/sec but TTFT p95 ~210ms which is higher than we expected from the demo.
- We warm the model cache between tests but saw a 2–3x difference when requests had 1k tokens vs 128 tokens (our average is 350).
- We used the public endpoint and a 2-second request timeout.

We can join a repro call on Wed Mar 25 afternoon. Also included a short script we used (repro_steps_k6.txt).

—Samir

Subject: Fwd: MAP kickoff — performance evaluation scope and close timeline — logs attached for repro

Team — forwarding ACME's logs and their k6 script. Key asks from ACME: match TTFT p95 and validate throughput at concurrency 4/8/16. Samir saw unexpected p95 TTFT ~210ms and throughput ~420 tokens/sec at concurrency ~8 for their workload (avg seq ~350 tokens).

Notes / immediate hypotheses:
- Tooling mismatch: k6 vs our internal bench harness (we use a batching-aware loadgen that simulates token streaming and KV cache warming). k6 default may not simulate identical TCP keepalive or chunked streaming semantics.
- Request shape: their 350-token average with occasional 1k token spikes will affect batching / kernel selection and can amplify TTFT variance.
- Endpoint: they hit public endpoint; need to confirm region/variant and model version pinned (they should be on redwood-v2-13b-int8 as demo’d).

Rishi — can you attempt a repro using their k6 script but instrumented to capture per-request headers (x-request-id) and our server-side trace ids? Also please collect split of time spent: network, scheduler queue, kernel execution, and token emission.

Connor — please pair with Rishi and prepare a short doc we can share with ACME showing how harness differences (k6 vs Redwood loadgen) cause measurement delta and recommended config for parity.

Marissa — FYI from MAP/ops side; if we see a config change that materially affects unit economics we can propose updated MAP entry.

Thanks — Neha
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>, Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>

Date: Tue, 24 Mar 2026 09:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: MAP kickoff — performance evaluation scope and close timeline — logs attached for repro

Team / Samir — I reproduced ACME's k6 workload in our staging region and compared it to our internal loadgen. Summary of findings:

- Reproduction result (k6): at concurrency=8 we measured ~390–430 tokens/sec; TTFT p95 was 200–230ms. Numbers align with ACME logs within noise.
- Internal loadgen (Redwood batching-aware): at equivalent offered load, we measured ~610 tokens/sec and TTFT p95 ~120–140ms. The difference is driven by two main causes:
  1) k6 opens N parallel HTTP connections and does not simulate chunked streaming token emission by default. Our runtime benefits from TCP keepalive and streaming which reduces perceived TTFT.
  2) Batching behavior — our internal harness coalesces concurrent requests into larger micro-batches if they arrive within a short window; k6's request timing spread reduces batching and increases per-token cost and TTFT.

- Model config: when we pinned the model to redwood-v2-13b-int8 and enforced identical max_tokens and stop sequences, the delta shrank but did not disappear. Sequence length heterogeneity (350 median, 1k spikes) causes kernel choice shifts and affects throughput non-linearly.

Actionable next steps:
- Connor / I will produce a short parity checklist (attached repro_steps_k6.txt + notes) that lists exact headers, connection settings, and a small wrapper to simulate streaming (chunked response).
- For the MAP: propose we record both harness numbers but mark the customer-observed metric as the gating metric. We'll include recommended config changes (enable streaming, use connection: keep-alive, and a small windowed batching shim) so ACME can reproduce the improved numbers without changing model behavior.
- I'll open INF-7783 to track the triage and include server-side trace ids so ACME can map client logs to our traces.

I'll be on the call Wed Mar 25 at 2pm PT to walk through the repro.

—Rishi
Senior Performance Engineer, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: MAP kickoff — performance evaluation scope and close timeline — logs attached for repro

Samir / Priya — thanks for joining the call. Attached is a short parity checklist and a small k6 wrapper we ran in staging that simulates chunked token streaming and TCP keepalive. Quick notes from the call:

- With the wrapper, ACME's k6 workload on the same endpoint produced ~580 tokens/sec at concurrency=8 and TTFT p95 ~135ms. That matches our internal harness within expected variance.
- Key settings: HTTP/1.1 chunked transfer, connection: keep-alive, per-request header x-redwood-session to enable consistent routing to the same worker for caching benefits.
- Remaining delta at p99 appears tied to sequence length spikes (1k tokens). We recommended two mitigations: 1) soft limit client-side to 800 tokens for tail requests, 2) enable prefix/KV caching for common instruction prompts.

Updated MAP items:
- Add a measurement row for harness-parity and include both k6-with-wrapper and Redwood-loadgen numbers.
- Agreement: ACME will run the wrappered k6 by Mar 26 and share updated logs. Redwood will run a production-matched test by Mar 27 and provide final MAP entry by Mar 30.

Files attached: repro_steps_k6.txt, summary_parity_checklist.pdf

Connor O'Brien
